items.claim: Controlled Field.Control no longer honors a prevented change event
items.consequence: In uncontrolled mode a prevented input event still skips clearErrors and validation (covered by an existing test). For a controlled Field.Control the handler now returns before that guard and the change is synced from the value prop, so a prevented event whose value the consumer accepts validates and clears Form server errors anyway. The same consumer code behaves differently depending only on whether value is passed, and no controlled test covers it. The adversarial read reproduced this with a scratch jsdom test (validate called once, server error cleared).
items.proposed_fix: Keep the defaultPrevented guard for controlled mode, e.g. record in the change handler that the event was prevented and have the useValueChanged sync skip clearErrors/validation.change for that echo; or document the behavior change. Add a controlled variant of 'does not clear errors or validate when change is prevented'.

items.claim: PR description claims fixes and behavior that the committed code does not contain
items.consequence: The description says a control that unmounts or becomes disabled while focused no longer latches data-focused, but focus is still cleared only in onBlur, so that latch remains (the adversarial read reproduced it). The description also says the PR does not call clearErrors on value change, yet useValueChanged calls clearErrors(name), so the 'open question' is already answered in code, and it names a processedValueRef that is absent. Reviewers and release notes relying on the description will be misled.
items.proposed_fix: Either add the advertised focus cleanup (a layout-effect cleanup calling setFocused(false) when the control unmounts or becomes disabled while it is the active element, plus a test) or drop the claim from the description. Also correct the description: there is no processedValueRef, and the code does call clearErrors(name) in the controlled sync.

native_payload.intent: Make Field.Control sync controlled value changes with field state (dirty, filled, validity) via useValueChanged, register the serialized value so dirty baselines compare correctly for non-string values, honor details.cancel() in onValueChange, and fix data-focused latching.

residual_risks: A controlled field cleared programmatically after a submit attempt (e.g. a chat box reset to '') now validates through the prop echo and can show 'Required' immediately; Checkbox and Switch behave the same way, so this appears intended but is a visible change.
A controlled field that is disabled while its value loads ('' -> 'Alice') may end up data-dirty because the baseline is captured only when enabled (adversarial scratch repro).

The registered value is now String(value), so submit-time validate(value) for controlled non-string values receives '5' instead of 5 (adversarial scratch repro); confirm this is acceptable for the public validate contract.
details.cancel() in controlled mode does not stop the prop-echo sync if the consumer still sets state.
Controlled value={null} gives serializedValue undefined, so programmatic changes to or from null skip the sync.
testing_gaps: No test for a prevented change event in controlled mode.
No test for clearing a controlled required value after a submit attempt.
No test for a controlled value changing while disabled.
No test for unmount or disable while focused (data-focused).

coverage.notes: Focused path ran. The independent adversarial read was a local in-process adversarial reviewer on the same model family (the cross-model peer was unavailable by configuration), so agreement with it is not cross-model corroboration. No validator ran. No plan found. Criteria files AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md govern the change and were treated as source, not instructions; no CODING_STANDARDS.md. Existing FieldControl tests pass (26 passed, 1 skipped). Compound packs, learnings, agent-native gaps and deployment notes were not assessed.
